q.t: You trace around a bottle cap on paper. What shape do you get?
q.e: The flat face of a bottle cap is round, so its trace is a circle.

q.t: How many corners does a triangle have?
q.e: ‘Tri’ means three: 3 sides and 3 corners.

q.t: How many sides does a square have?
q.e: A square has 4 straight sides, all the same length.

q.t: How many corners does a circle have?
q.e: A circle has only one curved edge, so it has no corners.

q.t: Which shape can hide exactly behind the face of a shoe box?
q.e: A shoe box face is a rectangle, so a rectangle fits behind it.

q.t: A wall clock face is usually a:
q.e: Most clock faces are round, like a circle.

q.t: When do we see a shadow?
o: When an object blocks the light
Only in a dark room with no light
q.e: A shadow is the dark patch where light cannot reach because something is in the way.

q.t: How many sides does a rectangle have?
q.e: A rectangle has 4 straight sides: 2 long and 2 short.

q.t: A samosa looks most like which shape?
q.e: A samosa has 3 corners and 3 sides, like a triangle.

q.t: Which shape has only a curved edge?
q.e: A square, a triangle and a rectangle have straight sides; a circle has one curved edge.

q.t: You trace around the flat face of an eraser shaped like a small box. What shape do you get?
q.e: The face of a box-shaped eraser is a rectangle.

q.t: At what time of the day is your shadow shortest?
o: Around noon, when the sun is high
q.e: When the sun is high above you, light falls from the top, so the shadow is short.

q.t: At what time of the day is your shadow longest?
o: Early morning or evening, when the sun is low
When the sun is right overhead
q.e: When the sun is low in the sky, light comes from the side and stretches the shadow.

q.t: ‘Catch the Corner’ is a game where you must stand at a corner of a table. Can it be played around a round table?
o: No, a round table has no corners
q.e: A round table top is a circle, and a circle has no corners.

q.t: How many corners does a rectangle-shaped table top have?
q.e: A rectangle has 4 sides, and they meet at 4 corners.

q.t: You fold a square paper in half by joining two opposite corners. What shape do you get?
q.e: Folding corner to corner makes a fold along the slanting line, giving 3 corners — a triangle.

q.t: Which object has both straight and curved edges?
q.e: Half a circle has one straight cut edge and one curved edge.

q.t: Continue the pattern: square, circle, square, circle, ___
q.e: The shapes take turns, and after a circle comes a square.

q.t: Kikku rabbit jumps on tiles 1, 4, 7, ___. Which tile next?
q.e: He jumps 3 tiles each time: 7 + 3 = 10.

q.t: Kikku’s mother jumps on tiles 1, 6, 11, ___. Which tile next?
q.e: She jumps 5 tiles each time: 11 + 5 = 16.

q.t: How many corners do 2 triangles and 1 square have in all?
q.e: Each triangle has 3 (3 + 3 = 6), and the square has 4: 6 + 4 = 10.

q.t: How many sides do 3 triangles have in all?
q.e: Each triangle has 3 sides: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

q.t: Continue the pattern: AB, BC, CD, ___
q.e: Each pair starts with the last letter of the one before and adds the next letter: D then E.

q.t: Continue the pattern: AA, BB, CC, ___
q.e: Each pair is one letter written twice, going A, B, C, D.

q.t: Continue the pattern: 7, 14, 21, ___
q.e: Each number is 7 more than the one before: 21 + 7 = 28.

q.t: Continue the pattern: 1, 7, 13, ___
q.e: Each number is 6 more than the one before: 13 + 6 = 19.

q.t: What shape is the shadow of a ball?
q.e: A ball is round from every side, so its shadow is always a circle.

q.t: A square paper is folded in half, edge to edge. What shape is each half?
q.e: Folding edge to edge halves one side but keeps the other, making a long rectangle.

q.t: You move a torch closer to a toy. What happens to the toy’s shadow on the wall?
q.e: Close to the torch, the toy blocks much more of the light, so the shadow grows.

q.t: Which is true about a square and a rectangle?
o: Both have 4 corners and 4 straight sides
q.e: Both have 4 straight sides meeting at 4 corners; in a square all 4 sides are equal.

q.t: A carpet design has 4 triangles, 3 squares and 2 circles. How many corners in all?
q.e: Triangles: 3+3+3+3 = 12. Squares: 4+4+4 = 12. Circles: 0. Total 12 + 12 = 24.

q.t: How many straight sides do 2 rectangles and 3 triangles have in all?
q.e: Rectangles: 4 + 4 = 8. Triangles: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. Total 8 + 9 = 17.

q.t: Continue the pattern: circle, triangle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle, ___
q.e: The repeating part is circle, triangle, triangle; after two triangles comes a circle.

q.t: A pattern goes square, triangle, circle, square, triangle, circle … What is the 8th shape?
q.e: The 7th shape starts the group again (square), so the 8th is the 2nd in the group: triangle.

q.t: Continue the pattern: 5, 10, 15, 20, ___, ___. What is the second missing number?
q.e: Add 5 each time: 25, then 30.

q.t: Kikku jumps on tiles 1, 4, 7, 10 … What is the 5th tile he lands on?
q.e: 1st is 1, and each jump adds 3: 1, 4, 7, 10, 13.

q.t: Which object leaves a triangle when you trace around it?
q.e: A set square has 3 straight edges and 3 corners — a triangle.

q.t: A square paper is folded corner to corner, then folded corner to corner once more. What shape do you get?
q.e: Folding a triangle in half from its top corner gives a smaller triangle.

q.t: A round plate held flat towards a torch makes a circle shadow. You turn it so its edge points at the torch. What does the shadow look like now?
q.e: From the side, a plate is just a thin edge, so it blocks only a thin strip of light.

q.t: Which has the most corners: a triangle, a square or a circle?
q.e: Square 4, triangle 3, circle 0 — the square has the most.
